definitions.explanation: The chemical, physical, and biological characteristics of water, typically evaluated to determine its suitability for drinking, swimming, agriculture, or environmental health.

examples.japanese: {水質|すいしつ}{検査|けんさ}を{行|おこな}う。
examples.english: To conduct a water quality test.

examples.japanese: この{川|かわ}の{水質|すいしつ}は{良好|りょうこう}だ。
examples.english: The water quality of this river is good.

examples.japanese: {工場|こうじょう}の{排水|はいすい}が{原因|げんいん}で、{周辺|しゅうへん}の{水質|すいしつ}が{悪化|あっか}している。
examples.english: The water quality in the surrounding area has deteriorated due to factory wastewater.

notes:
Composed of {水|すい} (water) and {質|しつ} (quality). A key term in environmental science and public health. Water quality monitoring is an important part of environmental protection in Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {水質|すいしつ}{検査|けんさ}: water quality testing
- {水質|すいしつ}{汚染|おせん}: water pollution
- {水質|すいしつ}{基準|きじゅん}: water quality standards
- {水質|すいしつ}が{悪化|あっか}する: water quality deteriorates
- {水質|すいしつ}{改善|かいぜん}: water quality improvement

RELATED TERMS:
- {水質|すいしつ}{汚濁|おだく}: water contamination — a more technical term for water pollution
- {浄水|じょうすい}: water purification / purified water
- {下水|げすい}: sewage — wastewater
- {飲料水|いんりょうすい}: drinking water
